title: Assignment 10 · Definiteness, preliminary agreements, and precontractual liability
summary: Definiteness, preliminary agreements, and precontractual liability. Assigned readings and principal cases for this class.
notes:
Dixon v. Wells Fargo, N.A.: A lender’s specific instructions to default while it considered a loan modification supported a promissory-estoppel claim, although the borrowers had no promise of a particular modified loan.

Cyberchron Corp. v. Calldata Systems Development, Inc.: Assurances to continue producing customized equipment supported reliance damages despite the parties’ failure to agree on weight requirements and penalties.

Channel Home Centers, Division of Grace Retail Corp. v. Grossman: A sufficiently definite and supported agreement to negotiate exclusively and in good faith can bind parties before they have agreed on the final lease.

Sun Printing & Publishing Ass’n v. Remington Paper & Power Co.: The majority refused to enforce future paper deliveries because both the future price and the period for which that price would operate remained to be agreed.

Oglebay Norton Co. v. Armco, Inc.: A long-term shipping contract remained enforceable after both pricing mechanisms failed because the evidence showed that the parties intended their underlying commitment to continue.

Additional assigned materials: Tribune preliminary-agreement discussion, C&M pp. 190–191; French Civil Code Article 1112.
